After the scandal, the minister was forced to ___.
items.explanation: “step down” = to leave an important job or position. Full sentence: After the scandal, the minister was forced to step down.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
She's had a difficult year, but I'm sure she'll ___.
items.explanation: “bounce back” = to recover quickly after a difficulty. Full sentence: She's had a difficult year, but I'm sure she'll bounce back.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
What does the abbreviation 'CEO' ___?
items.explanation: “stand for” = to be a short form of a word or name. Full sentence: What does the abbreviation 'CEO' stand for?

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
The committee invited residents to ___ ideas for the new park.
items.explanation: “put forward” = to suggest an idea or plan for people to consider. Full sentence: The committee invited residents to put forward ideas for the new park.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
Doctors did several tests to ___ a serious infection.
items.explanation: “rule out” = to decide that something is not possible or suitable. Full sentence: Doctors did several tests to rule out a serious infection.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
The bank will ___ paper statements over the next two years.
items.explanation: “phase out” = to gradually stop using or providing something. Full sentence: The bank will phase out paper statements over the next two years.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
After a stressful day, I need time to ___ before I can sleep.
items.explanation: “wind down” = to relax after a period of work or activity. Full sentence: After a stressful day, I need time to wind down before I can sleep.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
Some traditional companies still ___ employees wearing jeans to work.
items.explanation: “frown on” = to disapprove of something. Full sentence: Some traditional companies still frown on employees wearing jeans to work.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
My parents didn't want me to study art, but they've slowly ___ the idea.
items.meaningVi: dần chấp nhận, đổi ý ủng hộ
items.explanation: “come round to” = to change your opinion and accept an idea you disagreed with. Full sentence: My parents didn't want me to study art, but they've slowly come round to the idea.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
Your argument would be stronger if you could ___ it with some statistics.
items.meaningVi: chứng minh, củng cố (bằng chứng cứ)
items.explanation: “back up” = to provide evidence that shows something is true. Full sentence: Your argument would be stronger if you could back up it with some statistics.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
The new phone failed to ___ customers' high expectations.
items.explanation: “live up to” = to be as good as people expected. Full sentence: The new phone failed to live up to customers' high expectations.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
The company tried to ___ the seriousness of the data leak.
items.meaningVi: giảm nhẹ, làm như không quan trọng
items.explanation: “play down” = to make something seem less important or serious than it is. Full sentence: The company tried to play down the seriousness of the data leak.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
Hotels always try to ___ big sporting events by raising their prices.
items.meaningVi: kiếm lợi từ, tận dụng để trục lợi
items.explanation: “cash in on” = to make money or gain an advantage from a situation. Full sentence: Hotels always try to cash in on big sporting events by raising their prices.

items.question:
Choose the correct phrasal verb:
I hope the deal doesn't ___ at the last minute.
items.explanation: “fall through” = to fail to happen as planned. Full sentence: I hope the deal doesn't fall through at the last minute.
